title: California Public Records: A Technical and Legal Reference for the Post-AB 473 Era
description: A technical and legal reference to California's public-records ecosystem, anchored by the California Public Records Act (CPRA), recodified by Assembly Bill 473 effective January 2023 to Government Code §§ 7920.000 et seq., and extended in practice through state and local open-data portals, request platforms, API frameworks (CKAN, Socrata, ArcGIS), metadata schemas, intergovernmental data-sharing surfaces, and exemption rules.

methods.name: Registry-first compilation of CPRA statutes, portals, exemptions and datasets
methods.description: Held every cited section number, portal URL, schema field and dataset in Python registries under src/, with prose counts resolved from them at build time.
methods.evidence: every section number, portal URL, schema field, and dataset cited in the prose comes from a Python registry under src/

methods.name: Standard-library Python clients for California API surfaces
methods.description: Wrote working clients for CKAN Action API, Socrata SoQL, ArcGIS GeoServices REST, CIMIS REST, OpenJustice CSV and LegiScan endpoints.
methods.evidence: CKAN Action API, Socrata SoQL, ArcGIS GeoServices REST, CIMIS REST, OpenJustice CSV downloads, and LegiScan bulk-data endpoints, each with a working Python client in src/clients/

methods.name: Metadata-schema validators (DCAT, CKAN, Dublin Core, RIPA stop data)
methods.description: Implemented schema validators that accept a mapping and return a report of missing fields and warnings.
methods.evidence: Four schema validators live under src/schemas/. Each accepts a Python Mapping and returns a ValidationReport with ok, missing, and warnings fields.

methods.name: Offline no-mocks test suite with optional live endpoint checks
methods.description: Validated registries, clients and schemas against a real local HTTP server, plus optional live checks against California open-data endpoints.
methods.evidence: are validated by an offline no-mocks suite against a real local HTTP server, plus optional live checks against California open-data endpoints

methods.name: Cross-vendor citation verification (leginfo, Justia, FindLaw)
methods.description: Source-verified statute citations against leginfo and re-confirmed selected ones via Justia and FindLaw, removing those that could not be verified.
methods.evidence: a later cross-vendor audit re-confirmed selected citations against Justia and FindLaw where leginfo was network-blocked; citations that could not be independently verified were removed rather than carried as conjectures.

key_findings: The reference compiles California's public-records ecosystem into a machine-readable artifact: 22 CPRA statute sections, 17 portals, 7 exemption clusters and an 8-dataset OpenJustice taxonomy.
It notes that the AB 473 recodification made no substantive changes to disclosure rights but split the exemption list into independent code sections for readability.
Top-line verdict is 'CERTIFY-WITH-RESIDUALS': four CPRA sections from the upstream research document were misattributed or unverifiable and deliberately omitted.
A scaffolded citation-laundering example was rejected: § 7928.200 does not govern peace-officer records, so that mandate is pinned to Penal Code § 832.7.
The package's generator methods are pure functions of the registries, so re-running them yields byte-identical output apart from a single provenance timestamp.
key_findings_evidence: 22 registered CPRA statute sections across 5 structural categories; 17 open-data and request portals across 7 hosting platforms and 10 subject-matter domains; 7 exemption clusters, including 1 balancing-test and 6 categorical clusters
The reorga- nization made no substantive changes to disclosure rights but split the formerly monolithic exemption list into multiple independent code sections, improving readability and navigation

Residuals: four CPRA sections cited in the upstream research document (Gov. Code §§ 7922.650, 7923.200, 7927.600 as “library patron records”, 7928.200 as “peace oﬀicer records”) were either misattributed or unverifiable
The peace-oﬀicer disclosure mandate is therefore pinned to Penal Code § 832.7 rather than carried as a Government Code companion claim.
Re-running any of them yields byte-identical output except a single provenance timestamp, a property enforced by tests/test_idempotency.py

summary_provenance.method: Evidence-grounded extraction from full_text.md: every method and finding carries a verbatim quote from the paper text, mechanically verified to occur in full_text.md (whitespace/ligature-normalized) before merge.
summary_provenance.notes: Technical/legal reference with an accompanying software package, not an empirical study. The paper states its security controls beyond local ones are target posture, not present assurances.
